name: com.driftsys.dashscene
description: The C# side of dashscene. The boundary-B value types, the host that sits on the C ABI — version negotiation, runtime lifetime, document load, the tick and the committed frame — and the BatchRendererGroup painter that draws those tables. The macOS arm64 and Android arm64 libraries ship inside the package; the painter draws a subset of the document: this package's README lists what it draws and what it does not, and PackDiagnostic names the gap at run time rather than dropping it quietly.

samples.description: A MonoBehaviour that loads a .dsb, ticks it, hands each committed frame to BrgPainter and marks it drawn. Needs a host project meeting R-E4, R-E5 and R-E6 — a URP asset with the SRP Batcher on, and m_BrgStripping set to 2 — or the painter refuses to construct, or packs every instance and draws nothing.

The demonstration: the three corpus showcase scenes and several committed documents from a manifest in StreamingAssets, walked with the arrow keys or on a timer, with the rung, the instance count and every construct the painter refused reported on screen. Space runs a scene's own variant switch where it declares one. Needs the same host project R-E4, R-E5 and R-E6 describe. The scenes need a native producer the shipped library does not carry — they are built in Rust against a live arena, and no entry point on the shipped C ABI mutates a document — so a build without the DASHSCENE_DEMO_PRODUCER define draws the documents alone, which is what a customer's own build of this sample does. Importing it also sets Application.targetFrameRate to 60 at startup, process-wide; the CHANGELOG says why.
